newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end lower on weaker blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end lower on weaker blue chips.

text.p: Singapore shares closed lower on Wednesday as a short spurt of programme buying eased and left most blue chips weaker, dealers said.
"Property stocks are coming down after yesterday's programme buying subsided," said an institutional dealer with a foreign brokerage.
The SES Property Index fell 3.00 points to 685.17.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index was down 6.74 points at 2,182.31 after recovering from an intra-day low of 2,173.43.
The weakness in the broad market was reflected in number of losers overwhelming gainers, by 247 to 87. Market volume was moderate 105.83 million shares traded.
Top active Singapore Telecom 100 fell Singapore $0.10 to S$3.08 on a heavy volume of 7.15 million shares. SingTel dropped S$0.12 to S$3.10 and SingTel fell S$0.12 to S$3.06.

Dealers said people who had used money from their Central Provident Fund savings to buy stocks, but can only realise profits once a year, in October, were selling SingTel before the annual September 20 deadline.
Many predicted a technical rebound on Friday after the sell-down subsided.
